answer: Submissions that land within 138 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The atlas detector writes to spiral, and fable publishes every merge. A farm scripting its whole fleet fires them together, thus the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 67 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 27 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
